classification.difficultyReason: Translate an hourly temperature decrease into expressions, then evaluate after five hours.

content.prompt: The temperature in a room drops by $x^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ every hour. The temperature in the room at 12 p.m. is $25^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What will the temperature be at:

answer.worked:
One hour has elapsed.

$$\begin{align*}\text{New temperature}&=(25-1\times x)^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\\\text{New temperature}&=(25-x)^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\end{align*}$$

Six hours have elapsed.

$$\begin{align*}\text{New temperature}&=(25-6\times x)^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\\\text{New temperature}&=(25-6x)^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: If $x=6$, what will the temperature be at 5 p.m.?

answer.worked:
Five hours have elapsed.

$$\begin{align*}\text{New temperature}&=(25-5\times6)^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\\\text{New temperature}&=(25-30)^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\\\text{New temperature}&=-5^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\end{align*}$$

The $d$ values decrease by 3 whenever $t$ increases by 1. When $t=0$, $d=6$. Multiply $t$ by $-3$ and add 6.

The $n$ values increase by 3 whenever $m$ increases by 1. Each $n$ value is 3 less than three times $m$. Multiply $m$ by 3 and subtract 3.

entries.description:
The axes are called the coordinate axes or sometimes the Cartesian coordinate axes. They are named after the French mathematician and philosopher René Descartes (1596–1650). He introduced coordinate axes to show how algebra could be used to solve geometric problems. Although the idea is simple, it revolutionised mathematics.
Now we can imagine adding vertical and horizontal lines to the diagram through the integer points on the axes. We can describe each point where the lines meet by a pair of integers. This pair of integers is called the coordinates of the point. The first number is the horizontal coordinate and the second number is the vertical coordinate.

Remember, the first coordinate tells us where to go from the origin in the horizontal direction. If it is negative, we go to the left of the origin; if it is positive, we go to the right of the origin.
The second coordinate tells us where to go from the origin in the vertical direction. If it is negative, we go below the origin; if it is positive, we go above the origin.
We have labelled the horizontal axis the x-axis, and the vertical axis the y-axis.
The first coordinate is usually called the x-coordinate and the second coordinate is usually called the y-coordinate.
